newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end sharply lower as market corrects.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end sharply lower as market corrects.

text.p: Frozen concentrated orange juice futures closed sharply lower, tossing aside much of Monday's surprising gains but no fundamental news lay behind the correction, traders said.
Most-active July closed down 3.80 cents at 78.40 cents a lb, traded 81.30 to 78.00 cents. September through January 1999 ended 2.15 to 3.00 cents lower.
Volume was estimated at 5,000 lots against Monday's official 7,580 lots.
Some in the market were surprised by Monday's 6.80 cent rally despite a USDA upwardly revised forecast of a record 1996/97 crop in Florida.
Tuesday's dealings failed to muster follow through from Monday's overdone gains, dealers said.

"The trade was a good scale-up seller, and there was a little profit taking by locals from yesterday's run up. It's a go-figure type market," a broker said. "It looks like it wants to slip back down again."
Strong support in the July contract was pegged at 74.30 to 70.00 cents.
